_meta.purpose: Demand-side data for t-shirt concepts. `specificity_ladder` is the core tool: never generate at rung 0. `insider_vocab` supplies the belonging signal that makes a design convert.
_meta.ip_risk: R0 safe | R1 phrase check needed | R2 vibe-only, adjacent to protected IP | R4 forbidden

niches.name: Occupation / Profession
niches.audience: Working professionals buying for themselves, plus family buying gifts for them
specificity_ladder: new grad ICU nurse first year
niches.saturation: high at rung 0, medium at rung 2, low at rung 3
niches.notes: Gift buyers search the RELATIONSHIP plus the JOB: 'gift for nurse daughter'. Title must carry both.

niches.name: Pet Breed
niches.audience: Breed-specific owners; a genuinely obsessive, repeat-buying audience
insider_vocab: the orange one has one brain cell
niches.saturation: high for top-5 breeds, low-medium for rarer breeds and specific behaviours
niches.notes: Breed-plus-behaviour beats breed alone. Rarer animals face far thinner competition than popular breeds.

niches.name: Humour / Sarcasm
niches.audience: Self-purchase and gifting; the widest reach of any niche
specificity_ladder: I'm not arguing I'm just explaining why I'm right
the same joke told in the vocabulary of one specific subculture
insider_vocab: depends on the subculture - always draw from the target community's own phrasing
niches.saturation: very high for generic humour, medium for subculture-specific
niches.ip_risk: R1 — HIGH. Short phrases are exactly what gets registered as trademarks. Screen every phrase.
niches.notes: Insider, niche-specific humour outlasts generic funny. Meme trends decay fast - recency matters, and verify the joke isn't already well-executed on page one.

niches.name: Family Identity & Roles
niches.audience: Relationship-driven gifting - almost entirely bought by someone else
specificity_ladder: first Christmas as a bonus dad
niches.saturation: high for mom/dad, low-medium for regional grandparent names and step-parent roles
niches.notes: Regional grandparent naming (Gigi, Mimi, Pawpaw, Nonna, Yiayia, Abuela) is a large under-served long tail. Load 8-10 weeks before each gifting window.

niches.name: Hobbies & Subcultures
niches.audience: Enthusiasts who display their activity as an identity flag; loyal repeat buyers
niches.saturation: LOW-MEDIUM — the thinnest competition available. Highest priority lane.
niches.ip_risk: R0 for the activity; R1 for gear-brand references (never use them)
niches.notes: Real subculture vocabulary is the whole point - 'bouldering' over 'hiking'. Outsiders won't recognise the term, which is precisely what makes it convert.

niches.name: State / Regional Pride
niches.saturation: high for state names, low for specific towns, trails and rivers
niches.ip_risk: R1 — NEVER use university, team, or club names or colours in a varsity lockup. Invent the wordmark.

niches.name: Motivational / Mindset
niches.saturation: high for generic motivation, low-medium for sport-specific training vocabulary
niches.ip_risk: R1 — many fitness slogans and brand names are registered. Screen every phrase.

niches.name: Mental Health & Neurodivergence
niches.audience: Younger, expressive audience - strongest on Redbubble
specificity_ladder: the exact feeling, in original wording
niches.notes: Be specific and sincere rather than cliché. The exact feeling in original wording beats the slogan everyone has already done.

niches.name: Gaming & Anime VIBE (no names)
niches.audience: Gamers and anime fans; enormous demand, entirely closed to named IP
specificity_ladder: the specific feeling of grinding a turn-based random encounter at 2am
niches.ip_risk: R2 — VIBE ONLY. No franchise, character, studio, or item names anywhere, including tags and backend terms.
niches.notes: Design the vibe of a genre or community without any protected name, character, or logo. This is the single highest-volume lane that a POD seller can legally occupy.

niches.name: Music Scene Aesthetics (no band names)
niches.audience: Genre and scene loyalists; deep identity attachment
specificity_ladder: the visual language of a 1993 shoegaze 7-inch sleeve
niches.ip_risk: R2 — band names, logos, album art and lyrics are all protected. Design the FEEL of a scene only.
niches.notes: Lean on typography and mood. A genre's flyer aesthetic is not owned by anyone; a band's logo is.

niches.name: Values & Community Statements
niches.audience: People buying a public statement of belonging
insider_vocab: drawn from the specific community; avoid obvious clichés
niches.ip_risk: R1 — many campaign slogans are registered. Trademark-check every phrase.
niches.notes: Non-divisive framing sells far more broadly than partisan framing.

niches.name: Seasonal & Holiday
specificity_ladder: matching family christmas pyjama shirt for a family of five
gifting_windows: LOAD 8-10 WEEKS BEFORE THE DATE - this is the single most important rule in this niche
niches.saturation: very high in-season, low if you list early
niches.notes: Amazon and Etsy both need ranking runway. A Christmas design listed in November has already lost.
